cards.front: What should you know about graphic communication exam tips?
cards.back: Show FONT EXPERIMENTS — compare different typefaces for the same brief. Demonstrate understanding of hierarchy through varied weight, size and position. Annotate with type vocabulary.
Strokes at letter ends, varying thickness (e.g. Print body text, formal documents)
Clean, uniform stroke weight (e.g. Digital UI, signage, modern brands)
Bold, expressive, decorative (e.g. Headlines, posters, logos)
Mimics handwriting or calligraphy (e.g. Invitations, luxury branding)
Equal width for every character (e.g. Code, typewriter aesthetic, data)

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Using lots of different fonts makes a design more interesting and creative. Correct: Good typography uses a LIMITED palette of 1-2 font families. Too many fonts create visual chaos and look unprofessional. Create variety through WEIGHT, SIZE and CASE within one family instead.
Design a typographic poster using only letterforms (no images). Use typography to communicate a specific message, mood or theme. Annotate explaining your font choices, hierarchy and layout decisions.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Typography and Lettering
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Typography and Lettering using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

Typefaces are classified into broad families: Serif (Times New Roman, Garamond) have decorative strokes at letter ends; Sans-serif (Helvetica, Arial, Calibri) are clean without serifs; Display/Decorative (Impact, Lobster) are designed for headlines; Script (Brush Script) mimic handwriting; Monospace (Courier) have uniform character widths. Each classification communicates a different tone — serif

Typographic hierarchy uses size, weight, colour and position to guide the reader through content in order of importance. A typical hierarchy uses: H1 (large, bold, 24-36pt for titles), H2 (medium, semi-bold, 18-24pt for subtitles), body text (regular, 10-12pt for reading).
